ESV.1: And the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them, No one shall make himself unclean for the dead among his people,
ESV.2: except for his closest relatives, his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
ESV.3: or his virgin sister (who is near to him because she has had no husband; for her he may make himself unclean).
ESV.4: He shall not make himself unclean as a husband among his people and so profane himself.
ESV.5: They shall not make bald patches on their heads, nor shave off the edges of their beards, nor make any cuts on their body.
ESV.6: They shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God. For they offer the LORD's food offerings, the bread of their God; therefore they shall be holy.
ESV.7: They shall not marry a prostitute or a woman who has been defiled, neither shall they marry a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
ESV.8: You shall sanctify him, for he offers the bread of your God. He shall be holy to you, for I, the LORD, who sanctify you, am holy.
ESV.9: And the daughter of any priest, if she profanes herself by whoring, profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire.
ESV.10: “The priest who is chief among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil is poured and who has been consecrated to wear the garments, shall not let the hair of his head hang loose nor tear his clothes.
ESV.11: He shall not go in to any dead bodies nor make himself unclean, even for his father or for his mother.
ESV.12: He shall not go out of the sanctuary, lest he profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him: I am the LORD.
ESV.13: And he shall take a wife in her virginity.
ESV.14: A widow, or a divorced woman, or a woman who has been defiled, or a prostitute, these he shall not marry. But he shall take as his wife a virgin  of his own people,
ESV.15: that he may not profane his offspring among his people, for I am the LORD who sanctifies him.”
ESV.16: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.17: “Speak to Aaron, saying, None of your offspring throughout their generations who has a blemish may approach to offer the bread of his God.
ESV.18: For no one who has a blemish shall draw near, a man blind or lame, or one who has a mutilated face or a limb too long,
ESV.19: or a man who has an injured foot or an injured hand,
ESV.20: or a hunchback or a dwarf or a man with a defect in his sight or an itching disease or scabs or crushed testicles.
ESV.21: No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall come near to offer the LORD's food offerings; since he has a blemish, he shall not come near to offer the bread of his God.
ESV.22: He may eat the bread of his God, both of the most holy and of the holy things,
ESV.23: but he shall not go through the veil or approach the altar, because he has a blemish, that he may not profane my sanctuaries,  for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.”
ESV.24: So Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons and to all the people of Israel.

NASB.1: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: 'No one shall defile himself for a [dead] person among his people,
NASB.2: except for his relatives who are nearest to him, his mother and his father and his son and his daughter and his brother,
NASB.3: also for his virgin sister, who is near to him because she has had no husband; for her he may defile himself.
NASB.4: 'He shall not defile himself as a relative by marriage among his people, and so profane himself.
NASB.5: 'They shall not make any baldness on their heads, nor shave off the edges of their beards, nor make any cuts in their flesh.
NASB.6: 'They shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, for they present the offerings by fire to the LORD, the food of their God; so they shall be holy.
NASB.7: 'They shall not take a woman who is profaned by harlotry, nor shall they take a woman divorced from her husband; for he is holy to his God.
NASB.8: 'You shall consecrate him, therefore, for he offers the food of your God; he shall be holy to you; for I the LORD, who sanctifies you, am holy.
NASB.9: 'Also the daughter of any priest, if she profanes herself by harlotry, she profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire.
NASB.10: 'The priest who is the highest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to wear the garments, shall not uncover his head nor tear his clothes;
NASB.11: nor shall he approach any dead person, nor defile himself [even] for his father or his mother;
NASB.12: nor shall he go out of the sanctuary nor profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him; I am the LORD.
NASB.13: 'He shall take a wife in her virginity.
NASB.14: 'A widow, or a divorced woman, or one who is profaned by harlotry, these he may not take; but rather he is to marry a virgin of his own people,
NASB.15: so that he will not profane his offspring among his people; for I am the LORD who sanctifies him.''
NASB.16: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.17: 'Speak to Aaron, saying, 'No man of your offspring throughout their generations who has a defect shall approach to offer the food of his God.
NASB.18: 'For no one who has a defect shall approach: a blind man, or a lame man, or he who has a disfigured [face], or any deformed [limb],
NASB.19: or a man who has a broken foot or broken hand,
NASB.20: or a hunchback or a dwarf, or [one who has] a defect in his eye or eczema or scabs or crushed testicles.
NASB.21: 'No man among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a defect is to come near to offer the LORD'S offerings by fire; [since] he has a defect, he shall not come near to offer the food of his God.
NASB.22: 'He may eat the food of his God, [both] of the most holy and of the holy,
NASB.23: only he shall not go in to the veil or come near the altar because he has a defect, so that he will not profane My sanctuaries. For I am the LORD who sanctifies them.''
NASB.24: So Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel.

NKJV.7: They shall not take a wife who is a harlot or a defiled woman, nor shall they take a woman divorced from her husband; for the priest is holy to his God.

NKJV.9: The daughter of any priest, if she profanes herself by playing the harlot, she profanes her father. She shall be burned with fire.
NKJV.10: ‘He who is the high priest among his brethren, on whose head the anointing oil was poured and who is consecrated to wear the garments, shall not uncover his head nor tear his clothes;
NKJV.11: nor shall he go near any dead body, nor defile himself for his father or his mother;

NKJV.22: He may eat the bread of his God, both the most holy and the holy;
NKJV.23: only he shall not go near the veil or approach the altar, because he has a defect, lest he profane My sanctuaries; for I the LORD sanctify them.’ ”
NKJV.24: And Moses told it to Aaron and his sons, and to all the children of Israel.

AMP.1:
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them:
'No one shall defile himself [that is, become ceremonially unclean] for the dead among his people [by touching a corpse or assisting in preparing it for burial],
AMP.2: except for his relatives who are nearest to him, his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, and his brother,
AMP.3: also his virgin sister, who is near to him because she has had no husband; for her he may become unclean.
AMP.4: He shall not become unclean as a relative by marriage among his people, and so profane himself.
AMP.5: The priests shall not shave their heads, nor shave off the edges of their beards, nor make any cuts in their body.
AMP.6: They shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God; for they present the offerings by fire to the LORD, the food of their God; so they shall be holy.
AMP.7: They shall not take [as a wife] a woman who is a prostitute, nor a woman who is divorced from her husband; for the priest is holy to his God.
AMP.8: You shall consecrate him, therefore, for he offers the food of your God; he shall be holy to you; for I the LORD, who sanctifies you, am holy.
AMP.9: The daughter of any priest who profanes herself by prostitution profanes her father; she shall be burned in fire.
AMP.10: 'But he who is the high priest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to wear the [sacred] garments, shall not uncover his head nor tear his clothes [in mourning],
AMP.11: nor shall he approach any dead person, nor defile himself [by doing so, even] for his father or for his mother;
AMP.12: nor shall he go out of the sanctuary nor profane (make ceremonially unclean) the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him; I am the LORD.
AMP.13: He shall take a wife in her virginity.
AMP.14: He may not marry a widow or a divorced woman or one who is profaned by prostitution, but he is to marry a virgin from his own people,
AMP.15: so that he will not profane or dishonor his children among his people; for I am the LORD who sanctifies the high priest.'"
AMP.16: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.17: "Say to Aaron, 'Throughout their generations none of your descendants who has any [physical] defect shall approach [the altar] to present the food of his God.
AMP.18: For no man who has a defect shall approach [God's altar as a priest]: no man who is blind or lame, or who has a disfigured face, or any deformed limb,
AMP.19: or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand,
AMP.20: or a hunchback or a dwarf, or one who has a defect in his eye or eczema or scabs or crushed testicles.
AMP.21: No man among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a [physical] defect and is disfigured or deformed is to approach [the altar] to present the offerings of the LORD by fire. He has a defect; he shall not approach [the altar] to present the food of his God.
AMP.22: He may eat the food of his God, both of the most holy and of the holy things,
AMP.23: but he shall not go within the veil or approach the altar [of incense], because he has a defect, so that he will not profane My sanctuaries; for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.'"
AMP.24: So Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons, and to all the Israelites.

NLT.1: The LORD said to Moses, “Give the following instructions to the priests, the descendants of Aaron. “A priest must not make himself ceremonially unclean by touching the dead body of a relative.
NLT.2: The only exceptions are his closest relatives — his mother or father, son or daughter, brother,
NLT.3: or his virgin sister who depends on him because she has no husband.
NLT.4: But a priest must not defile himself and make himself unclean for someone who is related to him only by marriage.
NLT.5: “The priests must not shave their heads or trim their beards or cut their bodies.
NLT.6: They must be set apart as holy to their God and must never bring shame on the name of God. They must be holy, for they are the ones who present the special gifts to the LORD, gifts of food for their God.
NLT.7: “Priests may not marry a woman defiled by prostitution, and they may not marry a woman who is divorced from her husband, for the priests are set apart as holy to their God.
NLT.8: You must treat them as holy because they offer up food to your God. You must consider them holy because I, the LORD, am holy, and I make you holy.
NLT.9: “If a priest’s daughter defiles herself by becoming a prostitute, she also defiles her father’s holiness, and she must be burned to death.
NLT.10: “The high priest has the highest rank of all the priests. The anointing oil has been poured on his head, and he has been ordained to wear the priestly garments. He must never leave his hair uncombed or tear his clothing.
NLT.11: He must not defile himself by going near a dead body. He may not make himself ceremonially unclean even for his father or mother.
NLT.12: He must not defile the sanctuary of his God by leaving it to attend to a dead person, for he has been made holy by the anointing oil of his God. I am the LORD.
NLT.13: “The high priest may marry only a virgin.
NLT.14: He may not marry a widow, a woman who is divorced, or a woman who has defiled herself by prostitution. She must be a virgin from his own clan,
NLT.15: so that he will not dishonor his descendants among his clan, for I am the LORD who makes him holy.”
NLT.16: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.17: “Give the following instructions to Aaron: In all future generations, none of your descendants who has any defect will qualify to offer food to his God.
NLT.18: No one who has a defect qualifies, whether he is blind, lame, disfigured, deformed,
NLT.19: or has a broken foot or arm,
NLT.20: or is hunchbacked or dwarfed, or has a defective eye, or skin sores or scabs, or damaged testicles.
NLT.21: No descendant of Aaron who has a defect may approach the altar to present special gifts to the LORD. Since he has a defect, he may not approach the altar to offer food to his God.
NLT.22: However, he may eat from the food offered to God, including the holy offerings and the most holy offerings.
NLT.23: Yet because of his physical defect, he may not enter the room behind the inner curtain or approach the altar, for this would defile my holy places. I am the LORD who makes them holy.”
NLT.24: So Moses gave these instructions to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.

CSB17.1: The LORD said to Moses: “Speak to Aaron’s sons, the priests, and tell them: A priest is not to make himself ceremonially unclean for a dead person among his relatives, <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.2: except for his immediate family: his mother, father, son, daughter, or brother.
CSB17.3: He may make himself unclean for his unmarried virgin sister in his immediate family.
CSB17.4: He is not to make himself unclean for those related to him by marriage <sup>[1]</sup> and so defile himself.
CSB17.5: “Priests may not make bald spots on their heads, shave the edge of their beards, or make gashes on their bodies. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.6: They are to be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God. <sup>ⓕ</sup> For they present the fire offerings to the LORD, the food of their God, and they must be holy.
CSB17.7: They are not to marry a woman defiled by prostitution. <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓖ</sup> They are not to marry one divorced <sup>ⓗ</sup> by her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
CSB17.8: You are to consider him holy since he presents the food of your God. He will be holy to you because I, the LORD who sets you apart, am holy.
CSB17.9: If a priest’s daughter defiles herself by promiscuity, <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓘ</sup> she defiles her father; she must be burned to death. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.10: “The priest who is highest among his brothers, who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and has been ordained <sup>[4]</sup> to wear the clothes, must not dishevel his hair <sup>[5]</sup> or tear his clothes. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.11: He must not go near any dead person or make himself unclean even for his father or mother. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.12: He must not leave the sanctuary or he will desecrate the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him; <sup>ⓜ</sup> I am the LORD.
CSB17.13: “He is to marry a woman who is a virgin.
CSB17.14: He is not to marry a widow, <sup>ⓝ</sup> a divorced woman, <sup>ⓐ</sup> or one defiled by prostitution. He is to marry a virgin from his own people,
CSB17.15: so that he does not corrupt his bloodline <sup>[6]</sup> among his people, for I am the LORD who sets him apart.”
CSB17.17: “Tell Aaron: None of your descendants throughout your generations who has a physical defect <sup>ⓑ</sup> is to come near to present the food <sup>ⓒ</sup> of his God.
CSB17.18: No man who has any defect is to come near: no man who is blind, lame, facially disfigured, or deformed;
CSB17.19: no man who has a broken foot or hand,
CSB17.20: or who is a hunchback or a dwarf, <sup>[7]</sup> <sup>ⓓ</sup> or who has an eye defect, a festering rash, scabs, <sup>ⓔ</sup> or a crushed testicle. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.21: No descendant of the priest Aaron who has a defect is to come near to present the fire offerings to the LORD. He has a defect and is not to come near to present the food of his God.
CSB17.22: He may eat the food of his God from what is especially holy as well as from what is holy.
CSB17.23: But because he has a defect, he must not go near the curtain <sup>ⓖ</sup> or approach the altar. He is not to desecrate my holy places, for I am the LORD who sets them apart.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.24: Moses said this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.

MSG.1: God spoke to Moses: "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron. Tell them, A priest must not ritually contaminate himself by touching the dead,
MSG.2: except for close relatives: mother, father, son, daughter, brother,
MSG.3: or an unmarried sister who is dependent on him since she has no husband; for these he may make himself ritually unclean,
MSG.4: but he must not contaminate himself with the dead who are only related to him by marriage and thus profane himself.
MSG.5: "Priests must not shave their heads or trim their beards or gash their bodies.
MSG.6: They must be holy to their God and must not profane the name of their God. Because their job is to present the gifts of God, the food of their God, they are to be holy.
MSG.7: "Because a priest is holy to his God he must not marry a woman who has been a harlot or a cult prostitute or a divorced woman.
MSG.8: Make sure he is holy because he serves the food of your God. Treat him as holy because I, God, who make you holy, am holy.
MSG.9: "If a priest's daughter defiles herself in prostitution, she disgraces her father. She must be burned at the stake.
MSG.10: "The high priest, the one among his brothers who has received the anointing oil poured on his head and been ordained to wear the priestly vestments, must not let his hair go wild and tangled nor wear ragged and torn clothes.
MSG.11: He must not enter a room where there is a dead body. He must not ritually contaminate himself, even for his father or mother;
MSG.12: and he must neither abandon nor desecrate the Sanctuary of his God because of the dedication of the anointing oil which is upon him. I am God.
MSG.13: "He is to marry a young virgin,
MSG.14: not a widow, not a divorcee, not a cult prostitute—he is only to marry a virgin from his own people.
MSG.15: He must not defile his descendants among his people because I am God who makes him holy."
MSG.17: "Tell Aaron, None of your descendants, in any generation to come, who has a defect of any kind may present as an offering the food of his God.
MSG.18: That means anyone who is blind or lame, disfigured or deformed,
MSG.20: hunchbacked or dwarfed, who has anything wrong with his eyes, who has running sores or damaged testicles.
MSG.21: No descendant of Aaron the priest who has any defect is to offer gifts to God; he has a defect and so must not offer the food of his God.
MSG.22: He may eat the food of his God, both the most holy and the holy,
MSG.23: but because of his defect he must not go near the curtain or approach the Altar. It would desecrate my Sanctuary. I am God who makes them holy."
MSG.24: Moses delivered this message to Aaron, his sons, and to all the People of Israel.

NRSVCE.1: The LORD said to Moses: Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: No one shall defile himself for a dead person among his relatives,
NRSVCE.2: except for his nearest kin: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother;
NRSVCE.3: likewise, for a virgin sister, close to him because she has had no husband, he may defile himself for her.
NRSVCE.4: But he shall not defile himself as a husband among his people and so profane himself.
NRSVCE.5: They shall not make bald spots upon their heads, or shave off the edges of their beards, or make any gashes in their flesh.
NRSVCE.6: They shall be holy to their God, and not profane the name of their God; for they offer the LORD’s offerings by fire, the food of their God; therefore they shall be holy.
NRSVCE.7: They shall not marry a prostitute or a woman who has been defiled; neither shall they marry a woman divorced from her husband. For they are holy to their God,
NRSVCE.8: and you shall treat them as holy, since they offer the food of your God; they shall be holy to you, for I the LORD, I who sanctify you, am holy.
NRSVCE.9: When the daughter of a priest profanes herself through prostitution, she profanes her father; she shall be burned to death.
NRSVCE.10: The priest who is exalted above his fellows, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to wear the vestments, shall not dishevel his hair, nor tear his vestments.
NRSVCE.11: He shall not go where there is a dead body; he shall not defile himself even for his father or mother.
NRSVCE.12: He shall not go outside the sanctuary and thus profane the sanctuary of his God; for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is upon him: I am the LORD.
NRSVCE.13: He shall marry only a woman who is a virgin.
NRSVCE.14: A widow, or a divorced woman, or a woman who has been defiled, a prostitute, these he shall not marry. He shall marry a virgin of his own kin,
NRSVCE.15: that he may not profane his offspring among his kin; for I am the LORD; I sanctify him.
NRSVCE.16: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NRSVCE.17: Speak to Aaron and say: No one of your offspring throughout their generations who has a blemish may approach to offer the food of his God.
NRSVCE.18: For no one who has a blemish shall draw near, one who is blind or lame, or one who has a mutilated face or a limb too long,
NRSVCE.19: or one who has a broken foot or a broken hand,
NRSVCE.20: or a hunchback, or a dwarf, or a man with a blemish in his eyes or an itching disease or scabs or crushed testicles.
NRSVCE.21: No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall come near to offer the LORD’s offerings by fire; since he has a blemish, he shall not come near to offer the food of his God.
NRSVCE.22: He may eat the food of his God, of the most holy as well as of the holy.
NRSVCE.23: But he shall not come near the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a blemish, that he may not profane my sanctuaries; for I am the LORD; I sanctify them.
NRSVCE.24: Thus Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons and to all the people of Israel.

NIV.1:
Rules for Priests
The Lord said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: ‘A priest must not make himself ceremonially unclean for any of his people who die,
NIV.2: except for a close relative, such as his mother or father, his son or daughter, his brother,
NIV.3: or an unmarried sister who is dependent on him since she has no husband—for her he may make himself unclean.
NIV.4: He must not make himself unclean for people related to him by marriage, and so defile himself.
NIV.5: “‘Priests must not shave their heads or shave off the edges of their beards or cut their bodies.
NIV.6: They must be holy to their God and must not profane the name of their God. Because they present the offerings made to the Lord by fire, the food of their God, they are to be holy.
NIV.7: “‘They must not marry women defiled by prostitution or divorced from their husbands, because priests are holy to their God.
NIV.8: Regard them as holy, because they offer up the food of your God. Consider them holy, because I the Lord am holy—I who make you holy.
NIV.9: “‘If a priest’s daughter defiles herself by becoming a prostitute, she disgraces her father; she must be burned in the fire.
NIV.10: “‘The high priest, the one among his brothers who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and who has been ordained to wear the priestly garments, must not let his hair become unkempt or tear his clothes.
NIV.11: He must not enter a place where there is a dead body. He must not make himself unclean, even for his father or mother,
NIV.12: nor leave the sanctuary of his God or desecrate it, because he has been dedicated by the anointing oil of his God. I am the Lord.
NIV.13: “‘The woman he marries must be a virgin.
NIV.14: He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman defiled by prostitution, but only a virgin from his own people,
NIV.15: so he will not defile his offspring among his people. I am the Lord, who makes him holy.’”
NIV.17: “Say to Aaron: ‘For the generations to come none of your descendants who has a defect may come near to offer the food of his God.
NIV.18: No man who has any defect may come near: no man who is blind or lame, disfigured or deformed;
NIV.19: no man with a crippled foot or hand,
NIV.20: or who is hunchbacked or dwarfed, or who has any eye defect, or who has festering or running sores or damaged testicles.
NIV.21: No descendant of Aaron the priest who has any defect is to come near to present the offerings made to the Lord by fire. He has a defect; he must not come near to offer the food of his God.
NIV.22: He may eat the most holy food of his God, as well as the holy food;
NIV.23: yet because of his defect, he must not go near the curtain or approach the altar, and so desecrate my sanctuary. I am the Lord, who makes them holy.’”
NIV.24: So Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.

NET.1: The LORD said to Moses: “Say to the priests, the sons of Aaron — say to them, ‘For a dead person no priest is to defile himself among his people,
NET.2: except for his close relative who is near to him: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
NET.3: and his virgin sister who is near to him, who has no husband; he may defile himself for her.
NET.4: He must not defile himself as a husband among his people so as to profane himself.
NET.5: Priests must not have a bald spot shaved on their head, they must not shave the corner of their beard, and they must not cut slashes in their body.
NET.6: “‘They must be holy to their God, and they must not profane the name of their God, because they are the ones who present the LORD’s gifts, the food of their God. Therefore they must be holy.
NET.7: They must not take a wife defiled by prostitution, nor are they to take a wife divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
NET.8: You must sanctify him because he presents the food of your God. He must be holy to you because I, the LORD who sanctifies you all, am holy.
NET.9: If a daughter of a priest profanes herself by engaging in prostitution, she is profaning her father. She must be burned to death.
NET.10: “‘The high priest — who is greater than his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil is poured, who has been ordained to wear the priestly garments — must neither dishevel the hair of his head nor tear his garments.
NET.11: He must not go where there is any dead person; he must not defile himself even for his father and his mother.
NET.12: He must not go out from the sanctuary and must not profane the sanctuary of his God, because the dedication of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD.
NET.13: He must take a wife who is a virgin.
NET.14: He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or one profaned by prostitution; he may only take a virgin from his people as a wife.
NET.15: He must not profane his children among his people, for I am the LORD who sanctifies him.’”
NET.17: “Tell Aaron, ‘No man from your descendants throughout their generations who has a physical flaw is to approach to present the food of his God.
NET.18: Certainly no man who has a physical flaw is to approach: a blind man, or one who is lame, or one with a slit nose, or a limb too long,
NET.19: or a man who has had a broken leg or arm,
NET.20: or a hunchback, or a dwarf, or one with a spot in his eye, or a festering eruption, or a feverish rash, or a crushed testicle.
NET.21: No man from the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a physical flaw may step forward to present the LORD’s gifts; he has a physical flaw, so he must not step forward to present the food of his God.
NET.22: He may eat both the most holy and the holy food of his God,
NET.23: but he must not go into the veil-canopy or step forward to the altar because he has a physical flaw. Thus he must not profane my holy places, for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.’”
NET.24: So Moses spoke these things to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites.
